https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: An olive ridley sea turtle was observed laying eggs near Seal Beach in California on 16 September 2026. Photograph: City of Huntington Beach via Facebook View image in fullscreen An olive ridley sea turtle was observed laying eggs near Seal Beach in California on 16 September 2026. Photograph: City of Huntington Beach via Facebook California In historic first, tropical turtles spotted nesting on California beaches What caused the turtles to begin nesting farther north than usual is the ‘million dollar question’ Lois Beckett Wed 23 Sep 2026 20.32 EDT First published on Wed 23 Sep 2026 17.05 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A sea turtle crawled out of the surf in southern California last weekend around sunset and started laying eggs in the sand. People on Huntington Beach who saw the female olive ridley sea turtle were shocked and excited. And they weren’t the only ones freaking out, said Justin Viezbicke, the California stranding coordinator for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Association (Noaa). “This is the first documented case of a turtle nesting on the west coast,” Viezbicke said. What made the sighting even more noteworthy is that two different olive ridley sea turtles were identified laying eggs on Orange county beaches in the last week, the first on Seal Beach and the second on Huntington Beach. It’s a pattern that has scientists questioning whether the nestings are a freak occurrence, or the beginnings of a more lasting trend. US coast guard suspends search for man who reportedly jumped off cruise ship Read more While early news reports suggested that a single female turtle laid eggs on both California beaches, scientists further analyzed photographs of the turtles’ shell shape and barnacle patterns and determined that two separate olive ridley turtles had begun nesting on the US coast, Viezbicke said. Olive ridley turtles typically lay their eggs on beaches much further to the south, in Mexico and Central America, Viezbicke said. What caused the turtles to begin nesting further north than usual is the “million dollar question”, he said. Scientists are examining several different theories, including the environmental factor of warmer coastal waters, to other effects of El Niño, or whether the turtles “could have been blown off course by the recent hurricane”. “There’s been a lot of activity in the Pacific Ocean,” Viezbicke said. While it’s too soon to tell, it’s also possible that these first recorded US coastal nests could herald a broader northward shift in the olive ridley turtle’s nesting patterns, one driven by climate crisis and the warming ocean waters in the turtles’ native nesting areas, said Lance Adams, an aquarium veterinarian at the Aquarium of the Pacific in Long Beach. The sex of the olive ridley turtle is determined by temperatures where the eggs hatch, and warmer temperatures produce more female turtles. “After about 87.8F, they’re almost all female,” Adams said. To achieve a balanced population, the sea turtles might need access to cooler nesting areas. On the other hand, it’s hard to generalize from just two sightings, Adams said: “The turtles could be here by mistake.” Because the nesting season is not over and individual olive ridley turtles typically lay multiple nests of eggs, “We might see additional sea turtles making beach crawls to nest in the next 30 to 90 days,” Adams said. For protection, the new turtle nests have been surrounded by fencing. But there’s only so much local officials can do to protect the eggs, which typically take 45 to 60 days to hatch, Viezbicke said. It’s not just the dangers from local predators, such as coyotes, or from interfering humans. New hurricane swells and high tides are expected as soon as Monday of next week, Viezbicke said – and there’s a risk of the extreme weather “washing away that part of the beach”. Californians who spot sea turtles on a local beach should not interfere with them, and should keep at least 50 ft away, Adams, the aquarium veterinarian, advised. To advise authorities of a new turtle sighting, tell a lifeguard, or call Noaa’s marine animal stranding hotline , he recommended. Getting close to the turtles’ fenced-off nesting spots is not a good idea, he said: “People won’t see anything.” If locals want to observe live sea turtles in action, they can visit rescued turtles on display in rehabilitation tanks at an aquarium. Olive ridley sea turtles are one of the most abundant turtle species worldwide , but are protected under the US endangered species act . Warmer ocean temperatures have led to sightings of all kinds of sea creatures that aren’t typically spotted on the California coast, he noted, including different shark species, rays, sea horses and the venomous yellow-bellied sea snake. People should aim to adapt to shift in wildlife patterns, and, in general, keep their distance, Adams said, though new unexpected species present different potential risks. “Turtles aren’t particularly dangerous to humans. They can bite. They can slap with their flippers. Someone could potentially get hurt, but probably not seriously,” he said. https://www.theguardian.com/environment/.text: Authorities have warned against swimming in areas surrounding the dead whale after it was towed out to sea from the Clarence River. Photograph: Jessica Hromas/The Guardian View image in fullscreen Authorities have warned against swimming in areas surrounding the dead whale after it was towed out to sea from the Clarence River. Photograph: Jessica Hromas/The Guardian Australian climate and environmental reporting Australia news Authorities issue shark warning over whale that swam 11km upstream in Clarence River and later died Juvenile humpback was spotted near Bundjalung national park in what experts say is a rare but not unprecedented event Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Supported by About this content Petra Stock Mon 5 Oct 2026 01.02 EDT Last modified on Mon 5 Oct 2026 01.53 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google While the case of a whale found 11km upstream in a New South Wales river this weekend was unusual, it was not unprecedented, experts say. The juvenile humpback, which swam into the Clarence River on the state’s mid-north coast and later died, was towed out to sea on Sunday, according to NSW authorities. Members of the public first reported a sick whale swimming into the river near Bundjalung national park on Saturday afternoon. “The whale subsequently swam on to a sandbar and became grounded in shallow water, and within 30 minutes observers indicated the whale had died,” a spokesperson for NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service said. Increased shark activity in the surrounding area had been reported, with beachgoers advised to avoid surfing, swimming, or diving at surrounding beaches, SharkSmart NSW said in a post to social media. Whale scientist Dr Vanessa Pirotta said while the circumstances were rare, whales were known to explore rivers and estuaries from “time to time”. This could be the result of “misadventure” or “curiosity”, or due to ill health, as appeared likely for the animal in Clarence River, which looked “extremely unwell”. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email Most whales wouldn’t be aiming for the river at this time of year, she said. “Right now the main bulk of the east and the west coast populations are heading south to Antarctica. They’re on their way back for their summertime extended Christmas dinner where they’ll be going to Antarctica to feed on krill.” Earlier this year, in April, another whale became stranded on a sandbar in Wallis Lake on the NSW coast after swimming under the Forster Tuncurry Bridge. Last year, two humpbacks swam under Melbourne’s West Gate Bridge and into the mouth of the Yarra River. In 2020, three humpback whales entered the East Alligator River in Kakadu national park, with one travelling 30km upstream. All three eventually made their way back out to sea. While these air-breathing mammals could survive in freshwater environments, it probably wasn’t good for their skin, Pirotta said. Anyone spotting a whale in an unusual location such as a river, or an animal that appeared to be in distress, should alert environmental authorities, she said. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion Whales on Australia’s ‘humpback highway’ are at growing risk of injury from boat and propellor strikes Read more A spokesperson for Orrca, the cetacean rescue organisation , said while it was unusual for a whale to travel several kilometres into a river system, it was not unprecedented. “Humpback whales regularly travel close to the NSW coastline and may enter bays, harbours and estuarine environments temporarily during their annual migration.” Based on the large number of barnacles and other organisms on its skin, the juvenile in the Clarence River could have been experiencing a chronic illness, injury or another underlying health issue, the spokesperson said. “However, the cause of death cannot be determined from imagery alone,” they noted. “Each year, approximately 50,000 humpback whales migrate along Australia’s east coast. Across a population of this size, it is unfortunately not uncommon for a small proportion of animals to be observed in poor body condition or displaying other signs of illness, injury or compromised health.” The unusual event occurred less than a week after a humpback whale carcass washed ashore at Perth city beach, attracting multiple sharks before the body was removed on Thursday. “As with any deceased marine animal, people should avoid entering the water close to the location of the whale carcass, including surrounding beaches, and follow any local warnings or closures that may be in place. Whale carcasses can attract scavengers, including sharks,” the Orrca spokesperson said. https://24.hu/belfold/2026/11/11/varga-j.text: Korábban már Hack Péter jogtudóst, egyetemi tanárt, korábbi országgyűlési képviselőt, Szabó Máté volt ombudsmant és Fiszter Zsuzsannát , a Mi Hazánk Mozgalom végrehajtási és hitelügyi szakértőjét is meghallgatta a Toroczkai László Mi Hazánk-elnök vezette testület, mely 1994-ig visszamenőleg folytat vizsgálatot. A bizottsági elnök szerint hetvenhez közelít a meghallgatni kívánt személyek száma, ezért lesznek, akiket személyesen és lesznek, akiket írásban kérdeznek. Ennek indokaként azt hozta fel, hogy érzékelik az ügyben a társadalom „sürgető nyomását”, ezért nem javasolja a testület december végéig tartó mandátumának meghosszabbítását. A meghallgatásokon kívül adatokat is bekértek a Magyar Bírósági Végrehajtói Kartól, a Magyar Országos Közjegyzői Kamarától és a Szabályozott Tevékenységek Felügyeleti Hatóságától is. A bizottság a végrehajtói rendszer 1994-es, profitérdekeltté történő átalakításától kezdődően fogja vizsgálni a folyamatok működését. Szimbolikus és konkrét ügyként kezelik a Schadl–Völner-ügyet. A cél a rendszerszintű problémák feltárása, valamint a jogi és politikai felelősség megállapítása. Platón Szókratész védőbeszéd éből származó idézettel kezdte Varga Judit a megszólalását. Szerinte Früch Pál nyilvánvalóvá tette a vizságlóbizottság egy korábbi ülésén, hogy semmi köze a Völner-Schadle-ügyhöz. „Ki fog ezért tőlem bocsánatot kérni” – tette fel a kérdést, szerinte ugyanis folytatólagos rágalmazást követtel el ellene. „Pont egy olyan embert támadnak nemtelen eszközökkel, aki mindennap egy vidéki magyar ember szorgalmával és becsületével munkálkodott a nemzete boldogulásáért” – mondta. Toroczkai László, a vizsgálóbizottság elnöke néhány perccel 14 óra után megnyitotta az ülést. Jelezte, hogy Molnár Zoltán képviselő helyett Kiss Máté Zsolt lesz jelen. Az egyetlen napirendi pont Varga Judit és Répássy Róbert meghallgatása. Toroczkai elmondta, hogy először a meghallgatottaké lesz a szó, majd körönként minden képviselő két kérdést tehet fel nekik. Varga Judit megérkezett a meghallgatásra, mely hivatalosan 14 órakor kezdődik. Kezet fogott a jelenlévőkkel, és elfoglalta a helyét a teremben, Répássy Róbert mellett. Nem ez az egyetlen parlamenti vizsgálóbizottság, mely szeretné meghallgatni Varga Juditot. Az egykori igazságügyi minisztert a kegyelmi botrány felelőseit feltáró bizottság is szeretné beidézni . Csakúgy, mint Novák Katalin volt köztársasági elnököt és Balog Zoltánt, a volt államfő tanácsadójának meghallgatását is javasolja Schummer Orsolya, a testület tiszás elnöke.

Ukraine: Dramatic night rescue pulls woman from rubble after 22 hours Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 23 November 2026 - 11:17 GMT+1 An elderly woman was rescued alive after spending 22 hours trapped beneath concrete slabs in Dymer, north of Kyiv. The death toll from Sunday's Russian strike on an apartment building has risen to 11. … More After spending 22 hours trapped beneath concrete slabs , 79-year-old Valentyna was pulled alive from the wreckage of a five-storey apartment building in Dymer, north of Kyiv , devastated by a Russian drone strike . Found on the first floor, she was handed to paramedics and taken to hospital, offering a rare moment of relief amid the destruction . ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Under the glare of floodlights, rescuers searched through mountains of broken concrete and twisted metal , while sniffer dogs combed the ruins for survivors. Emergency workers carried injured residents to ambulances, recovered bodies from the rubble and even brought a cat to safety. Ukraine's State Emergency Service announced the rescue on Monday, as the death toll climbed to 11 and two people remained missing . The attack, which struck overnight on 22 November, destroyed part of the residential block, leaving emergency crews working through the night in search of anyone still buried beneath the rubble .
